newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA'S GROWTHPOINT UPS INCOME 11.1 PCT.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA'S GROWTHPOINT UPS INCOME 11.1 PCT.

text.p: South African property loan stock company Growthpoint Properties Ltd recorded consistent earnings growth in the year ending March 31, 1997.

Net income before debenture interest and taxation grew by 11.1 percent to 20.4 million rand while combined income per unit for the year grew by 11.1 percent to 60 cents, the company said in a statement.
Turnover, reflecting rent receivable from tenants, grew by 16 percent to 27.6 million rand.
Growthpoint's Jeffrey Sher said this was due to higher rentals as well as the 12.5 million rand acquisition of the Otjiwarongo shopping centre in Namibia on April 1 last year.
Occupancy levels in the commercial and retail portfolio remained at 95 percent. Interest income declined by 27 percent as a result of the acquisition, the company said.
Growthpoint recently announced a partial redemption of debentures to the value of 100 million rand.

Sher said the rationale was to unlock value for Growthpoint shareholders who have seen the share price languish at less than 50 percent of net asset value, which he described as a common problem in this sector.
Growthpoint had raised a 100 million rand loan from Investec Bank Ltd , which it would use to redeem debentures and repay shareholders at a rate of 2,94 rand per unit, he said.
The loan from Investec would be repaid over the next 12 to 15 months from the proceeds of the sale of buildings earmarked for this purpose, he added.
"We expect the redemption to enable shareholders to unlock the value of their shareholding, and we hope to narrow the gap between net asset value and share price to less than 25 percent," Sher said.
